answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history. Before an agent can trade at full limits, it must lock a deposit and complete useful, checkable tasks over time, building a reputation that flows like a river of past performance rather than a single fresh claim. Creating many fake identities then costs many deposits plus sustained work, while an honest agent reuses one history. Trust deepens gradually, like pigment that only darkens with repeated dyeing, so a sudden lotus-like bloom of new accounts earns no instant privilege and is easy to rate-limit.
